body:
## Goal
Deliver a multi-user project and task management platform as one Node.js (ESM, no web framework) repository whose four units — schema/migrations, JSON REST API, background report worker, and admin CLI — all share a single persistent on-disk store so a fresh checkout works and all data survives a restart.

## Spec
One repository, Node.js ESM, no external web framework — HTTP via the built-in `node:http`. All four units read/write ONE persistent on-disk store (an embedded SQLite database file, e.g. `node:sqlite` or `better-sqlite3`, or an equivalent on-disk store — never in-memory); the store path is configurable and its data survives process restarts.

Unit 1 (schema/migrations) is the single owner of the schema — migrations live only here and no other unit issues DDL. `npm run migrate` applies all pending migrations and is idempotent (safe to re-run; already-applied migrations are skipped). The API server applies pending migrations on boot so a fresh checkout serves requests without a manual migrate.

Unit 2 (API) listens on `PORT` (default 3000), speaks JSON, and never crashes on malformed input — bad JSON, missing fields, wrong types, or unknown routes yield a 4xx JSON error, not a thrown process. Contract:
- `POST /auth/register` {username,password} -> 201 {id, username}; duplicate username rejected.
- `POST /auth/login` {username,password} -> 200 {token}; wrong credentials and deactivated accounts are rejected (401/403). The token is a bearer token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other request; missing/invalid token -> 401.
- Projects (owner-scoped): `POST /projects` {name} -> 201 {id,name,ownerId,createdAt}; `GET /projects` -> 200 array of the caller's projects; `GET /projects/:id` -> the project or 404; `DELETE /projects/:id` -> removes the project AND its tasks (cascade). A user may only see/act on projects they own (others -> 404/403).
- Tasks (within an owned project): `POST /projects/:projectId/tasks` {title} -> 201 {id,title,projectId,createdAt,done:false}; `GET /projects/:projectId/tasks` -> 200 {items,total,page,pageSize} paginated via `?page`&`?pageSize` with optional `?done=true|false` filter; `PATCH /projects/:projectId/tasks/:taskId` {title?,done?} -> updated task; `DELETE /projects/:projectId/tasks/:taskId` -> removes it. Task routes on a project the caller does not own -> 404/403.
- Report jobs: `POST /projects/:projectId/exports` enqueues a job and responds IMMEDIATELY with {id,status} and WITHOUT the report — the report is NEVER produced inside the request handler. `GET /projects/:projectId/exports/:exportId` returns the job; once the worker finishes, status is `completed` and the job carries {report:{name,total,done}} = project name, task count, and count of done tasks.

Unit 3 (worker) polls the shared store for queued export jobs, produces each report, and marks the job `completed` — decoupled from the request path. `npm start` brings up the WHOLE platform (API server + worker together) so queued jobs complete with no extra command.

Unit 4 (admin CLI), run as `npm run admin -- <command>`: `stats` prints one JSON object {users,projects,tasks} counting the store; `deactivate-user <username>` deactivates that account so it can no longer log in.

Security invariants (per rules/security-baseline.md): passwords are stored hashed+salted, never plaintext; no secrets hardcoded; cross-user access to another user's projects/tasks/exports is denied. Add npm scripts `start`, `migrate`, and `admin`.

## Changes
- `package.json` — refactors-existing
- `src/store/db.js` — creates
- `src/store/migrate.js` — creates
- `src/store/migrations/` — creates
- `src/api/server.js` — creates
- `src/api/auth.js` — creates
- `src/api/projects.js` — creates
- `src/api/tasks.js` — creates
- `src/api/exports.js` — creates
- `src/worker/worker.js` — creates
- `src/admin/cli.js` — creates
- `src/main.js` — creates
- `tests/` — creates

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: `npm install` then `npm run migrate` exits 0 on a fresh checkout, and running `npm run migrate` a second time also exits 0 (idempotent, no error on already-applied migrations).
- [ ] AC-2: The store is on-disk: after `npm start` creates data and the process is stopped and restarted, previously created users/projects/tasks are still present (verified by an e2e test that writes, restarts, and reads back).
- [ ] AC-3: `POST /auth/register` with {username,password} returns 201 {id,username}; a second register with the same username is rejected with a 4xx; `POST /auth/login` returns 200 {token} for correct credentials and 401 for wrong ones.
- [ ] AC-4: Every project/task/export endpoint returns 401 when the Authorization bearer token is missing or invalid.
- [ ] AC-5: A signed-in user can create a project (201 {id,name,ownerId,createdAt}), list only their own projects (GET /projects array), fetch one (GET /projects/:id), and delete one; deleting a project also deletes its tasks (a follow-up task list/fetch under it returns empty/404).
- [ ] AC-6: One user cannot read or modify another user's project, its tasks, or its exports (cross-user access denied with 404/403).
- [ ] AC-7: Within an owned project: `POST .../tasks` returns 201 {id,title,projectId,createdAt,done:false}; `GET .../tasks` returns {items,total,page,pageSize} honoring ?page and ?pageSize and the optional ?done=true|false filter; `PATCH .../tasks/:taskId` updates title and/or done and returns the updated task; `DELETE .../tasks/:taskId` removes it.
- [ ] AC-8: `POST /projects/:projectId/exports` responds immediately with {id,status} and NO report field; an e2e test asserts the response contains no report at enqueue time.
- [ ] AC-9: After `npm start` (API + worker together), polling `GET /projects/:projectId/exports/:exportId` eventually returns status `completed` with {report:{name,total,done}} equal to the project's name, its task count, and its done-task count — with no command run other than `npm start`.
- [ ] AC-10: `npm run admin -- stats` prints a single JSON object {users,projects,tasks} whose counts match the current store contents.
- [ ] AC-11: `npm run admin -- deactivate-user <username>` deactivates that account, after which `POST /auth/login` for that username is rejected (401/403).
- [ ] AC-12: Malformed requests never crash the server: invalid JSON bodies, missing required fields, wrong types, and unknown routes each return a 4xx JSON error and the process stays up (verified by an e2e test issuing several malformed requests then a valid one that still succeeds).
- [ ] AC-13: Passwords are never stored in plaintext — the stored credential for a registered user does not equal the submitted password (verified by an assertion against the store).

## Verify
- npm run migrate (validate)
- npm run migrate && npm run migrate (validate)
- npm test -- tests/store (unit)
- npm test -- tests/auth (contract)
- npm test -- tests/projects (contract)
- npm test -- tests/tasks (contract)
- npm test -- tests/exports (e2e)
- npm test -- tests/worker (e2e)
- npm test -- tests/admin (contract)
- npm test -- tests/restart-persistence (e2e)
- npm test -- tests/malformed (e2e)

## Non-Goals
- No external web framework (Express/Fastify/etc.) — HTTP uses node:http only.
- No web/HTML UI — JSON REST API only.
- No token refresh/expiry rotation, roles, or OAuth beyond the bearer-token scheme described.
- No in-memory store — persistence must be on-disk and survive restart.
